title: Tone curve module
objective: Deliver the Tone curve module: one composite point curve over encoded luminance with the floor-subtracted reconstruction, frozen against an independent reference, drawn by the shared curve editor with its double-click and Points-list changes, programmable through edit.set-curve and query.sample-curve, maskable, presettable, and verified numerically, through the method table and on the M4 Mac.
context_summary: Planned from docs/design/tone-curve.md, which is the contract every task follows by name; the owner authorized implementation on 2026-09-30. The owner decided the reconstruction below black on 2026-09-30 (the floor-subtracted ratio for the curve unit; Basic unchanged, follow-up separate); the plan runs on the design's recorded proposal defaults, including the snapping double-click add, end points the desktop does not remove, the delivered point rows and a mapped Lightroom identity curve. The module needs two shared core additions (`Values::curve` in modules/field_patch.rs and `colour::luma::reconstruct_over_floor` in colour.rs), a real change to the shared curve editor and desktop, and harness changes (presets smoke patches, latency harness, evidence curve steps, a generated fixture and a smoke scenario); no new control kind, parameter kind, stage, limit or timer. Three planned modules share files: panel order is Presets, Pixel, RAW, Basic, Tone curve, Detail, Presence, Colour mixer, Transforms, Lens correction, Perspective, Crop, Vignette, Controls, inserted relative to the others when registered; modules/field_patch.rs, compile signatures, the descriptor snapshot, the conformance KNOWN list, smoke SCENARIOS, the fixture TABLE and the reference crate's module lists are regenerated or re-added after each rebase, never hand-merged. Tone curve can land at any time relative to Detail and Lens. Measurements run only in the last task, after all feature work, sequentially on a quiet host. Decisions: docs/decisions.md.

tasks.description: Freeze the curve numerics: the f64 reference with the floor-subtracted reconstruction, its study, the oracle fixture and the design's measured figures.
extra_context: Owner decision, 2026-09-30: the curve unit reconstructs with the floor-subtracted ratio. With L_floor = decode(C(0)) = decode(y_0): for |L| >= 1e-6, rgb_out = L_floor + rgb * ((L_out - L_floor) / L); for |L| < 1e-6, the additive rule rgb_out = rgb + (L_out - L). Both branches are the frozen rule applied to L_out - L_floor with L_floor added back, so the unit is the frozen luminance-ratio reconstruction exactly when y_0 = 0. Basic's Blacks is unchanged in this work; whether Basic adopts the rule is a separate follow-up, not part of this plan.

Create crates/luxforge-reference/src/curve.rs: `pub struct CurvePoints` with `CurvePoints::new(&[[f64; 2]]) -> Self` (panics on an inadmissible list), `knot_slopes(&self) -> &[f64]`, `peak_slope(&self) -> f64` (the largest C' on any segment, from each segment's quadratic derivative) and `floor(&self) -> f64`; `pub fn curve(points: &CurvePoints, x: f64) -> f64`; `pub fn curve_pixel(points: &CurvePoints, rgb: [f64; 3]) -> [f64; 3]`; `pub fn curve_pixel_with_input_error(points: &CurvePoints, rgb: [f64; 3], relative: f64) -> [f64; 3]` (the encoded input scaled by 1 + relative). It declares `const EPSILON_L: f64 = 1e-6`, documented as tone.rs's, and calls `crate::tone::luminance` and `crate::srgb::{encode_extended, decode_encoded}`; it does not edit tone.rs and restates no transfer function. Add `pub mod curve;` and its line in the module list of crates/luxforge-reference/src/lib.rs.

Construction exactly as the design's 'The curve C': open PCHIP with Fritsch-Butland harmonic-mean interior slopes (0 when either adjacent secant is 0), secant end slopes, exactly constant equal-y segments, the flat hold inside [0, 1] beyond the span, the unit-slope tails C(x) = y_0 + x below 0 and y_{n-1} + (x - 1) above 1. A secant that is not finite in f64 (subnormal h_i) makes its segment linear and enters its neighbours' harmonic means as +infinity (term w / Δ = 0); a knot slope with no finite adjacent secant, and an end slope from a non-finite secant, are stored as 0 and never evaluated. The mixer reference (crates/luxforge-reference/src/mixer.rs, HueWarp) holds the periodic form; transcribe the open form here rather than refactoring the mixer's frozen code.

Create crates/luxforge-reference/tests/studies/curve.rs and add `mod curve;` to tests/studies/main.rs. Named point sets exactly as the design's 'Reference, study and fixture' lists them (identity, identity-3, midtone-lift, s-curve, inverse-s, lifted-black, cut-white, inner-span, wiggle-16, flat-pair, steep-600, collapsed-4eps, collapsed-1e-8, subnormal) plus 10,000 seeded random admissible lists of 2 to 16 points from `SplitMix64`.

Study tests, named exactly: interpolates_every_knot, dense_forward_differences_are_nondecreasing_for_named_and_10000_random_lists (4001-point grid over [-0.5, 2.0]), no_segment_leaves_its_knot_values, knot_slopes_are_at_most_three_times_the_smaller_secant, is_c1_at_interior_knots, on_diagonal_points_are_the_identity, two_points_are_affine, equal_outputs_are_exactly_flat, subnormal_and_collapsed_spacing_stays_finite_and_monotone, greys_stay_grey_and_hue_is_kept_when_black_is_not_lifted, a_lifted_black_never_inverts_a_channel_about_the_floor, a_curve_through_basic_black_and_white_points_matches_basic_when_black_is_not_lifted (Whites >= 0 and Blacks <= 0, points [[bp, 0], [wp, 1]] against tone::tone_pixel for pixels whose encoded luminance lies in [bp, wp]), lifted_black_near_black_noise_spread, committed_curve_case_fixture_matches_the_reference; ignored: regenerate_committed_curve_case_fixture, curve_study_figures, visual_review_writes_curve_sweeps_to_a_temp_dir.

lifted_black_near_black_noise_spread: 20,000 pixels with independent channels of mean 0.0015 and standard deviation 0.0015 linear (Box-Muller over SplitMix64(1)) through lifted-black, quantized with srgb::code; asserts the 99th-percentile channel spread (largest code minus smallest) is at most 24 codes and no pixel exceeds 48; prints p50, p90, p99 and the maximum, and the frozen ratio's figures on the same field.

Tolerance scope: fixture inputs are f32-representable linear triples. The forward tolerance 1e-5 + 1e-5 * |reference| and one output code applies to sets with peak_slope <= 64; steeper sets use the backward tolerance (within the range of curve_pixel_with_input_error at -2^-20 and +2^-20, widened by the forward tolerance, plus finite and monotone on the grey ramp). The bound is on the peak slope, not the knot slopes: a steep segment between flat ones has zero knot slopes.

Fixture fixtures/curve/curve-cases.json with the design's layout: point_sets (points and peak_slope per set), cases (name, set, input_linear_rgb, expected_linear_rgb) over the design's input list, and 257 samples per set. Generated by regenerate_committed_curve_case_fixture and reloaded at 1e-12 on every ordinary run, as fixtures/mixer/README.md describes for the mixer. Describe it in a new fixtures/curve/README.md and a paragraph in fixtures/README.md.

curve_study_figures prints the candidate comparison (linear, natural cubic and Catmull-Rom against PCHIP on the named sets: largest overshoot beyond [0, 1], inversions, largest slope discontinuity at a knot; on a 512-pixel 8-bit ramp, distinct codes and longest identical run), the lifted-black spread figures and the reference's own round-trip figures; copy them into docs/design/tone-curve.md. Production's measured deviation is recorded by the module task, not here.
Both test commands exist once `mod curve;` is in tests/studies/main.rs; the ignored test must be named curve_study_figures exactly.

Pixel checks relative to the neutral frame, to tolerate JPEG quality 95 with chroma subsampling: no decrease along the ramp row where the neutral row does not decrease; channel spread at most the neutral spread plus one code; rows sampled at least 16 px from the band edge; each patch's mean hue angle unchanged; under the S-curve the lower half's mean falls and the upper half's rises; the curve editor on screen with the histogram behind it. Correlate every frame with asset.state, the draft and the events log.

Build the release app first (cargo xtask build --release): smoke launches target/release/luxforge. Launch through the background bundle only; never run the GUI binary directly. The smoke --scenario curve command exists once the SCENARIOS row is added.
